source.title: From Isolated Feature to Orbits: Discovering Music Concepts via Multi-SAE Alignment

record.tranche_reason: The study refines the idea that individual SAE features are stable, self-contained units: it reports variation in feature identities and local connections across runs, while the larger orbit semantics remain identifiable. It does not test superposition or feature-capacity claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports organized SAE feature orbits and explicitly notes that feature-level ambiguity remains. Only results relevant to whether SAE features are stable canonical units are included as rows. Its chord/key task scores and cited findings do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study argues and shows that musical concepts sit in structured groups of SAE features (orbits), not single features. Its seed-robustness and probe-vs-SAE analyses bear on whether individual SAE features are stable, complete units (V5). The models are music audio encoders, not LLMs, and the study does not test toy-model superposition or capacity accounts.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors argue that musical concepts are better read through transposition-induced orbits of SAE features than through isolated features. They report a previously unreported subdominant-centered ring in MuQ. They claim linear recoverability (e.g., tonic) does not imply an explicit concept, whereas SAEs capture salient sparse concepts. They state the method does not eliminate feature-level polysemanticity, but relational consistency reduces its impact.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses multi-SAE alignment under pitch transposition to recover music-concept orbits; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Orbit recovery and downstream results vary with model, layer, sparsity K, threshold τ, dataset, and random seed; the study reports some core orbits absent at particular settings.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features in music encoders form transposition-equivariant cyclic families (12-feature rings for major chords, minor chords, and a relative-major subdominant). Higher-level concepts correspond to the shared invariant of such a family rather than to a single feature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concepts are represented as structured families of SAE features related by known input transformations, rather than as isolated dictionary features.

record.problems: The evidence for feature stability and disentanglement includes qualitative visualizations and descriptions rather than uncertainty estimates. The study's models are music foundation models, and it does not test capacity-based superposition.
record.rows_left_out: Downstream chord/key scores and comparisons with probes or standard SAEs are omitted because they evaluate task performance, not whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units. Other orbit-discovery results likewise do not directly measure that version.

untested.parts: Canonicality across SAE sizes or architectures, and quantitative feature-level stability (no matching or overlap scores reported).
All of it: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry of superposition.
All of it: no capacity or importance analysis.
Not tested in LLMs; the models are music audio encoders (MuQ, MusicFM).
Not tested. Orbits are groups of ordinary 1-D SAE features; dimensionality of features is not examined.

missing.what: Linear probes detect tonic and dominant signals, but no corresponding standard-SAE features are found; only subdominant features appear (bears on dictionary completeness).
Recovery of the core orbits depends on layer, K and τ. No minor-chord orbit is recovered from MuQ layer 6 at any tested τ. The subdominant ring is found in MuQ but not MusicFM.

record.verdict_notes: Music foundation models are not LLMs, so V4 and V5 apply only by analogy to the 'real model' setting; V5 is treated as tested since it is not model-type specific. Evidence for stability is qualitative graph visualization, with no quantitative feature-matching scores. The authors' orbit-aware initialization and shared Top-K support are interventions that shape feature alignment, so cross-seed orbit stability partly reflects their inductive bias.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is evidence for superposition.
The version concerns LLMs; the study analyzes music foundation models and does not measure LLM feature distribution or SAE recovery.

Whether SAE dictionaries are complete, and whether features are canonical across models or training procedures. The study examines run-to-run stability of orbit structures and qualitative feature activations.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.

rows.subject: MuQ (2) o-SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared recovered orbit graphs across four random seeds.
rows.measure: Run-to-run stability of feature identities, local graph connections, and core orbit semantics
rows.value: Exact feature IDs and local graph connections vary across runs; major-chord, minor-chord, and subdominant structures remain identifiable.
rows.note: The text characterizes the semantic structures as reproducible up to feature permutation, rather than reporting stable individual feature identities.
rows.check: Link and state are fine. Varying feature IDs is expected permutation, so the substantive instability is in local graph connections. Orbit-level semantics remain identifiable across 4 seeds. Evidence is qualitative (Figure 19).

rows.subject: MuQ (2) o-SAE
rows.operation_detail: Inspected recovered-orbit activations on a POP909 excerpt in C minor.
rows.measure: Qualitative agreement and separation of orbit activations across chord segments
rows.value: Activations are broader and overlap more strongly across neighboring chord segments; some expected orbit–chord correspondences are weak or incomplete.
rows.note: The authors retain this as an example of imperfect disentanglement in realistic audio.
rows.check: A hand-picked qualitative example of imperfect disentanglement of orbit activations on one C-minor excerpt. It measures frame-level selectivity of orbit features, not completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features, so it does not bear on V5.

relationships.condition: MuQ layer 2 o-SAE, K=48, four random seeds
relationships.reason: Local orbit-graph connections vary across seeds; only coarse orbit semantics (major, minor, subdominant) stay identifiable (R1). Stability holds at group level, not as identical feature-level structure.
relationships.display_finding: Local orbit-graph connections varied across seeds and only coarse orbit semantics (major, minor, subdominant) stayed identifiable, so stability held at group level rather than as identical feature-level structure.

relationships.condition: Standard Top-K SAE (s-SAE) on MuQ/MusicFM, tonic and dominant key functions
relationships.reason: From the text (Sec 5.4.2, Fig 3), not a row: linear probes recover weak tonic/dominant signals that have no matching SAE features. The dictionary does not capture all linearly recoverable information. Authors read this as the concept not being explicit in the model.
relationships.display_finding: Linear probes recovered weak tonic and dominant signals that had no matching SAE features, so the dictionary did not capture all linearly recoverable information; the authors read this as the concept not being explicit in the model.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MuQ (2) o-SAE across the four reported random seeds and the C-minor POP909 excerpt
reader_labels.reason: Core orbit semantics persist across seeds, but individual feature identities and local connections vary; the C-minor activations also overlap and have incomplete correspondences (R1, R2). This supports stability at the orbit level, not canonicality or perfect separation of individual SAE features.
